title: Is free text web RPG games still a thing?
author: ExaminationKnown1103
selftext: I always like these kind of games, such as The Crims, and I was thinking to develop a free text game too. Is that still a thing? I noticed the The Crims is still out there with some audience, though.

comments.author: Xiaomin4114
comments.body:
These days the surviving text games are:  
\- fairly niche interactive fiction group. you can play a lot of these online, search for "interactive fiction online"

\- MUDs are still alive. less popular now, but they're like MMOs, but text-based

\- New generation of AI-based text RPG, I dunno about "free" though, it's actually fairly expensive to run to generate large-scale narratives. It's different to AI chat bots that just try to roleplay a character, AI generated fiction RPGs have to hold a plot, world persistence, and stuff, and takes quite a lot to do. I've been building one of these at [https://stagewhisper.ai](https://stagewhisper.ai) 

If you're going to build interactive fiction, AI will do most of that job for you no problems. But definitely give it a web interface, and sling it on [itch.io](http://itch.io) or something. I don't think many people will actively go download a game just for it to be text-based.

replies.author: ExaminationKnown1103
replies.body: Thanks! Interesting, I didn't know about MUD. Yeah, my idea is to build something similar to The Crims, purely web based, multiplayer, in the topic of resources management.

comments.author: PoorSquirrrel
comments.body:
It is, but it's become even more of a niche than it used to.

source: I started a (mostly) text web game 25 years ago and it's still around. But player counts used to be higher.

replies.author: ExaminationKnown1103
replies.body: That's nice, so you got quite some experience. Did you make some money out of it? Is it online? Can I access it?

replies.author: PoorSquirrrel
replies.body: I let people make donations, and later added a paid tier with some minor bonuses (like one additional character). It was enough to cover hosting and other costs, and for a hobby it was cool to have a small revenue flow. As a business it would've been a failure.

Give it a try.

comments.author: Arkanta
comments.body:
Like others said, I think this field is moving to AI. While not fully RPG, I've been dabbling in the creation of a "book you're the hero of" RPG (no hardcore rpg mechanics) with https://playimagina.com/ but keeping a free tier would be very hard.

For others, I've seen some text web RPGs being played over discord. You need to find a community, but they're quite active.
